title: Vaginal Birth After Caesarean: Intrapartum Care

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman with one or more previous caesarean births in labour in a Saudi hospital delivery suite who has chosen planned vaginal birth: suitable setting, admission assessment, continuous fetal monitoring and one-to-one care, pain relief including epidural, progress in labour, induction and oxytocin augmentation decisions, recognition and emergency response to uterine scar rupture, third stage, and conversion to caesarean. Uses the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guideline No. 45 with the oxytocin and antibiotic product labels and Saudi centre data; no Saudi national guideline was found.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology guideline on intrapartum care after caesarean was found; the RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 45 (2015) is a United Kingdom guideline and a newer edition may exist.

The oxytocin label (Pitocin) warns against use in women with previous caesarean 'except in unusual circumstances' and does not give a VBAC regimen; the start rate and step in the label are written, and the guideline's warning that rates above 20 milliunits per minute raise rupture risk four-fold is added. The decision to augment is a senior obstetrician decision.

Dinoprostone vaginal insert (Cervidil) and gel (Prepidil) labels list previous caesarean section as a contraindication, while the guideline states that low-dose prostaglandin E2 may be used with restricted dose under local rules; no prostaglandin regimen is written here, and mechanical induction (Foley catheter or amniotomy) is described as the lower-risk option. The Foley catheter is a device and has no medicine label.
Epidural analgesia is allowed by the guideline but no local anaesthetic regimen was reviewed, so none is written.

Cefazolin 1 g is the label prophylaxis dose; the guideline and NICE name cefuroxime with metronidazole before the incision for elective repeat caesarean, and the best agent for emergency caesarean after labour is a local policy choice.
Tranexamic acid, carbetocin, misoprostol and other postpartum haemorrhage medicines are not written here; refer to the postpartum haemorrhage pathway.
Antenatal counselling, elective repeat caesarean and long-term follow-up are in the antenatal counselling topic.
Figures were read by automated extraction of PDF and label text; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Labour contractions stretch the lower segment scar; rupture is most likely at 4 to 5 cm dilatation and more than 90% occur in labour (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1). Induction, especially with prostaglandins, and oxytocin augmentation raise the risk of rupture two- to three-fold (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2). Oxytocin at rates above 20 milliunits per minute raises rupture risk four-fold or more (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2). A rising need for epidural top-ups can signal impending rupture (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1). Rupture usually causes an abnormal fetal heart rate trace, pain, bleeding or maternal collapse; a baby delivered within about 18 minutes of suspected rupture has the best chance of avoiding hypoxia (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

symptoms: Severe abdominal pain, especially pain that continues between contractions (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Increasing pain or analgesia requirement (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Abnormal vaginal bleeding or blood in the urine (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Faintness, collapse or shortness of breath (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
physicalSigns: Abnormal cardiotocography, present in 66 to 76% of ruptures (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Scar tenderness of acute onset and loss of previously efficient contractions (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Maternal tachycardia, hypotension or shock (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Loss of station of the presenting part, change in abdominal contour or fetal heart not found at the old site (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
redFlags: Abnormal cardiotocography in a woman with a scar: act as for suspected uterine rupture, call the senior obstetrician and anaesthetist and prepare for immediate caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Severe constant pain, scar tenderness, bleeding or maternal shock: emergency laparotomy and neonatal resuscitation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Rising epidural dosing or sudden change in pain: examine for impending rupture (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Slow progress with adequate contractions: do not push with high-dose oxytocin; review for caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Cervical dilatation not progressing on the agreed parameters: stop VBAC and offer caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Collapse after vaginal birth with bleeding: consider rupture found after delivery (about 8% are identified after vaginal birth) and look for scar damage (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
precipitants: Induction of labour, particularly with prostaglandins, and oxytocin augmentation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
No previous vaginal birth, body mass index over 30, large baby, short interval since the last birth, age 40 or over (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.4).
Previous low vertical or inverted T incision (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 6.2).
Labour in a unit without immediate surgery or continuous monitoring (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Arriving in unplanned labour with no earlier counselling (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Abnormal cardiotocography with pain, bleeding or maternal instability; confirmed at laparotomy (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Painful bleeding with a hard tender uterus and fetal heart rate changes (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Slow cervical progress with weak or irregular contractions; may need review before augmentation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Pain relieved by a standard top-up; frequent dosing should prompt a search for rupture (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Abnormal trace without pain, bleeding or maternal change; still managed urgently (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess on arrival
actions: Confirm the previous caesarean history, the planned mode of birth and the counselling record (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1).
In unplanned labour, have an experienced obstetrician decide whether vaginal birth is feasible (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Admit to a delivery suite with immediate caesarean, anaesthetic and neonatal resuscitation available (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Start established-labour care
actions: Give one-to-one support and start continuous electronic fetal monitoring (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Site intravenous access and send full blood count and group and save (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Record maternal pulse, blood pressure, temperature, pain and bleeding regularly (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Assess cervical progress at least every 4 hours (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Offer pain relief
actions: Offer epidural if she wants it; it is not contraindicated (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Consider early placement of an epidural catheter in case of operative delivery (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Treat a rising need for top-ups or a change in pain pattern as a possible sign of rupture (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Manage slow progress
actions: Ask a senior obstetrician to review before oxytocin; check contraction strength and exclude obstruction (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Discuss augmentation with the woman, including a two- to three-fold higher rupture risk and the option of caesarean (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Use the lowest effective oxytocin rate and stop if progress is not made on the agreed parameters (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).

clinicalManagement.title: If labour was induced
actions: Offer induction only after senior obstetric assessment and counselling on the higher risks (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Prefer a mechanical method (Foley catheter or amniotomy) to prostaglandins when induction is chosen (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
If prostaglandin is used, restrict the total dose by local guideline (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Respond to suspected rupture
actions: Call the senior obstetrician, anaesthetist, neonatal team and theatre at once (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Stop oxytocin, resuscitate the mother and move to emergency laparotomy; aim to deliver within about 18 minutes (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Give pre-incision antibiotic if time allows and arrange blood (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1 and Section 9.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Deliver and manage the third stage
actions: Give oxytocin 10 units intramuscularly after delivery of the placenta (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration).
Examine the perineum and watch for bleeding or collapse, since about 8% of ruptures are found after vaginal delivery (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Record the mode of birth and outcome so the next counselling can use it (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 7.1).

regimens.indication: Stimulation of weak or infrequent contractions in planned vaginal birth after caesarean when the senior obstetrician has agreed
regimens.patientGroup: Women in labour after one previous lower segment caesarean with slow progress and inadequate uterine activity
regimens.dose: Start at 0.5 to 1 milliunit per minute (3 to 6 mL per hour of the dilute solution) and increase by 1 to 2 milliunits per minute every 30 to 60 minutes until a regular contraction pattern is reached; rates above 9 to 10 milliunits per minute are rarely needed at term (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration). Keep the rate as low as possible; do not exceed 20 milliunits per minute because rupture risk rises four-fold or more (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2). Dilution and preparation: add one 10-unit/1 mL vial to 1,000 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride or Ringer's lactate to give 10 milliunits per mL, and mix well by rotating the bottle; run through a separate line piggybacked as near the cannula as possible (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration).
regimens.route: Intravenous infusion by pump only; never as an intravenous bolus; the infusion is piggybacked on a separate line of plain electrolyte solution (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.frequency: Continuous infusion with the rate changed every 30 to 60 minutes
regimens.duration: Until adequate contractions are reached, then reduce once labour is at 5 to 6 cm; stop for hyperactivity, fetal distress or failure to progress (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration)
adjustments: Label warning: oxytocin should not be given except in unusual circumstances where there is a predisposition to uterine rupture such as previous caesarean; the decision lies with a senior obstetrician (Pitocin label, Precautions).

Do not use if there is significant cephalopelvic disproportion, fetal distress where delivery is not imminent, hypertonic uterus, total placenta praevia, vasa praevia or cord prolapse (Pitocin label, Contraindications).
Water intoxication risk with long infusions in large fluid volumes: monitor fluid balance (Pitocin label, Precautions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Continuous cardiotocography and uterine activity throughout the infusion (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration).
Stop immediately for uterine hyperactivity or fetal distress, give oxygen and place the mother in a lateral position (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration).
Pain, bleeding and cervical progress at the agreed intervals (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
contraindications: Significant cephalopelvic disproportion, unfavourable fetal position that cannot be corrected, fetal distress with delivery not imminent (Pitocin label, Contraindications).
Hyperactive or hypertonic uterus; invasive cervical cancer; active genital herpes; total placenta praevia; vasa praevia; cord presentation or prolapse (Pitocin label, Contraindications).

regimens.indication: Prevention of postpartum uterine bleeding after delivery of the placenta
regimens.dose: 10 units (1 mL) once, after delivery of the placenta (Pitocin label, Control of Postpartum Uterine Bleeding). Dilution and preparation: none for the intramuscular dose; if bleeding continues an intravenous infusion of 10 to 40 units in up to 1,000 mL of electrolyte solution may be used, with a maximum of 40 units per 1,000 mL (Pitocin label, Control of Postpartum Uterine Bleeding).
regimens.route: Intramuscular injection (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration); an infusion is used to sustain the contraction of the uterus
regimens.duration: Single intramuscular dose; infusion adjusted to keep the uterus contracted
adjustments: Check the uterus is contracted and bleeding is not excessive; scar rupture can present as bleeding after birth (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Water intoxication risk with prolonged infusion (Pitocin label, Precautions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Uterine tone, blood loss and blood pressure (Pitocin label, Adverse Reactions).
Signs of water intoxication with long infusions (Pitocin label, Adverse Reactions).
contraindications: Do not use the intramuscular dose before delivery of the placenta for induction (Pitocin label, Dosage and Administration).

regimens.indication: Prophylaxis against wound, urinary and womb infection before emergency caesarean or laparotomy
regimens.patientGroup: Women moving to caesarean after failed VBAC or suspected rupture without cephalosporin allergy
regimens.dose: 1 g as a single dose 30 to 60 minutes before the start of surgery, or as early as possible in an emergency (Cefazolin label, Perioperative Prophylactic Use). Dilution and preparation: reconstitute each 1 g vial with 2.5 mL of sterile water for injection (about 330 mg/mL), shake well; for direct injection dilute further with about 5 mL of sterile water and inject slowly over 3 to 5 minutes; for infusion dilute in 50 to 100 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose (Cefazolin label, Reconstitution and Administration).
regimens.route: Intravenous injection over 3 to 5 minutes or intravenous infusion; the label also allows intramuscular use
regimens.duration: Single dose; repeat only if the operation lasts 2 hours or more (Cefazolin label, Perioperative Prophylactic Use)
adjustments: Give before the skin incision; pre-incision prophylaxis reduces infection more than later dosing (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Do not use co-amoxiclav before the incision (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1).
Renal impairment: reduce the interval or dose for repeated dosing (Cefazolin label, Dosage).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Hypersensitivity during and after the injection (Cefazolin label, Warnings).
Diarrhoea after antibiotics may be Clostridioides difficile colitis (Cefazolin label, Warnings).
contraindications: Known allergy to the cephalosporin group of antibiotics (Cefazolin label, Contraindications).

regimens.sourceEdition: RCOG Green-top 45, Section 9.1; Cefazolin label, Perioperative Prophylactic Use and Reconstitution

medicationPlan.note: The choice and timing of medicines follow RCOG Green-top 45; doses, dilution, administration method and contraindications come from the product labels named in each row. Oxytocin is used here only on the decision of a senior obstetrician because the product label warns against use in women with a previous caesarean except in unusual circumstances. Dinoprostone products are contraindicated on their labels in women with a previous caesarean and no regimen is written. All doses are for adult women. SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Suitably staffed delivery suite with continuous care and monitoring, immediate caesarean and advanced neonatal resuscitation (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Continuous electronic monitoring from the onset of regular contractions (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
One-to-one support, intravenous access with full blood count and group and save, regular observations and cervical assessment at least every 4 hours (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).
Decision by a senior obstetrician with the woman, after explaining a two- to three-fold higher rupture risk (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).
Keep as low as possible; rates above 20 milliunits per minute raise rupture risk four-fold or more (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.2).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Time from suspected rupture to delivery
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Aim for delivery within 18 minutes (RCOG Green-top 45, Section 8.1).

teaching.scope: Woman with one or more previous caesarean births in labour in a Saudi hospital delivery suite who has chosen planned vaginal birth: suitable setting, admission assessment, continuous fetal monitoring and one-to-one care, pain relief including epidural, progress in labour, induction and oxytocin augmentation decisions, recognition and emergency response to uterine scar rupture, third stage, and conversion to caesarean. Uses the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Green-top Guideline No. 45 with the oxytocin and antibiotic product labels and Saudi centre data; no Saudi national guideline was found.
learningObjectives: Plan VBAC in a delivery suite with immediate caesarean and neonatal resuscitation.
Give one-to-one care, continuous monitoring, intravenous access and bloods, and assess cervix at least every 4 hours.
Use senior-led decisions for induction and oxytocin and keep the oxytocin rate low.
Act at once on abnormal cardiotocography, pain, bleeding or collapse.
pitfalls: Using high-dose oxytocin to correct slow progress.
Delay in calling the senior team.
Forgetting rupture can show after vaginal birth.
keyPoints: Abnormal cardiotocography is the commonest sign of rupture.
Epidural is allowed but rising top-ups are a warning.

patientEducation: We will watch your baby's heartbeat all the time and a midwife will stay with you.
Tell us at once about constant pain, bleeding, feeling faint or a change in your contractions.
You can have an epidural; tell us if the pain changes.
If labour slows, a senior doctor will talk to you about a drip or a caesarean.
If we need to move to a caesarean it is a planned safety step, not a failure.
You can change your plan at any time.
lifestyleAndDiet: Eat lightly and drink while in early labour as advised.
Move around as comfortable; keep the cannula secure.
Bring your hospital bag and previous operation records.
Have someone with you for support.
Rest and feed the baby soon after birth.
mdtReferrals: Obstetrician and gynaecologist (senior on call); midwife (one-to-one); anaesthetist; neonatologist or neonatal resuscitation team; theatre team; blood bank; pharmacist.
dischargeCriteria: Mode of birth and outcome documented; rupture or dehiscence ruled out; bleeding and uterine tone normal; analgesia, thromboprophylaxis and feeding plan given; postnatal care and contraception planned.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Postnatal care as for any woman after birth; document the outcome for counselling in a later pregnancy; review at 6 to 8 weeks.
